target_customer: Mobile-first consumers buying makeup, mainly younger women in the US
problem: Makeup shoppers wanted cheap, discoverable products on their phones; the founders found makeup was the only category selling significantly after trying general low-priced branded goods.
business_model: Mobile-first e-commerce retailer selling beauty products direct (retail margin)

founders.name: Alex Lin
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CEO with no background.

founders.name: William King
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CTO with no background.

founders.name: Cooper Mor
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page. Dealroom also names Ashwin Kamath as a founder, but the YC page does not, so he is not listed here.

exit.reason: Not stated; YC lists the company as inactive, Dealroom describes it in the past tense and tags it closed.

competitors.name: Wish
competitors.what: Mobile-first shopping app selling cheap products shipped from Chinese manufacturers
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch reported 'hundreds of millions of users' in March 2016
competitors.funding_then: $500M round led by DST Global reported in 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile commerce app with catalog, checkout and fulfillment is standard engineering. The hard parts were merchandising, sourcing and user acquisition cost, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Selling third party makeup through an app has no switching costs or proprietary supply, so Sephora, Ulta, Amazon and Wish could serve the same shoppers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sephora was already shipping mobile commerce experiments in 2016 such as its Kik bot and swipe-based shopping. No source describes an incumbent acting directly against Hush.

market_need_then: The founders reported (via Dealroom) that after launching a mobile store of low-priced brands, makeup was the only category with significant sales. Beauty was a large and fast-moving online category in 2016, but no independent demand source for Hush itself was found.

branding.domain_note: Used shophush.com, a prefixed domain; it now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, so the domain is parked or lapsed.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC copy claims 'the top social commerce app in the United States', an unverified boast.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand was found. Searches for the name return many unrelated Hush brands (UK fashion, sleep products), which shows the name is generic and confusable.

pivots.from: Mobile retail of various low-priced name-brand products
pivots.why: Makeup was the only category generating significant sales, per Dealroom (single database, date approximate).

outcome_analysis: Hush was a three founder Summer 2016 mobile makeup retailer from Los Angeles that pivoted from general low-priced goods to beauty. Only thin database data on funding exists and no shutdown cause is public, so failure factors are left empty. The category was crowded with Sephora, Ulta, Amazon and Wish and the model had little defensibility, but no source shows why the company went inactive.
notes: The 2018-11 seed round of $0.63M rests on a single database (CB Insights financials page seen only through search results, not opened because the page returned HTTP 403). The same search surfaced a different CB Insights Hush page reporting a $35M Series B in April 2018 and $42.6M total over 4 rounds; that conflicts with a two person startup and may be a different company called Hush, so it is not recorded as a round. Several unrelated companies share the name Hush. No press release or second outlet confirmed any round. Website shophush.com is a for-sale parked domain.
